incidents.vector: Network intrusions against the Philippine nuclear research agency and a major naval contractor; initial access method not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: Suspected Chinese state hackers breached the Philippine Nuclear Agency and a major naval contractor, exposing sensitive government and defense information.

incidents.vector: Data theft followed by a $3.3 million extortion demand; the stolen customer database was published when the company refused to pay.
incidents.impact: Data on almost 13 million customers was leaked online after Carhartt refused the ransom; the dataset also contained millions of synthetic fake records.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion into the vendor's systems followed by a failed extortion attempt.
incidents.impact: A new ransomware group breached Micro-Comm, maker of the SCADAview CSX system used by US water utilities, and leaked stolen company data after extortion failed.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to systems holding car park, lounge, Fast Track and airport Wi-Fi customer data; disclosed after the company refused a ransom demand.
incidents.impact: Data of about 8.7 million customers of Manchester, London Stansted and East Midlands airports was exposed, including email addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registrations and postcodes; no payment card data was taken and flights were unaffected.

incidents.victim: European government & diplomatic bodies (Romania, Spain, Türkiye)
incidents.vector: Spearphishing with macro-enabled Word documents using diplomatic lures that install a lightweight batch-script backdoor abusing legitimate webhook services for command and control.
incidents.impact: Campaigns from late September 2025 through April 2026 targeted defense manufacturing, government and diplomatic organizations, giving Russian military intelligence remote access for intelligence collection tied to Moldova's elections and NATO-adjacent governance.

incidents.vector: Social-engineering spear-phishing over Signal and WhatsApp, impersonating app support teams and using QR codes to link attacker devices to victims' accounts.
incidents.impact: The EU confirmed eight significant spear-phishing incidents against high-ranking officials in 2026; Germany's Bundestag President was among those breached, prompting EU governments to move to in-house messaging platforms.

incidents.victim: Global users of ZBT white-label routers
incidents.attacker: China — device manufacturer with embedded backdoors
incidents.vector: Root-level backdoors built into router firmware at the factory, beaconing out to manufacturer-controlled domains for remote command and control.
incidents.impact: Routers from Chinese manufacturer ZBT, resold under many brand names in over 50 countries, ship with implants allowing full remote control; infections are estimated in the six figures and 'fixed' devices were found still shipping with the backdoor.

incidents.vector: Seven custom remote-access tool families developed with AI assistance, using modular plug-ins and rotating infrastructure to evade detection and attribution.
incidents.impact: A disciplined cyberespionage operation is targeting Central Asian government networks; AI-assisted development lets the group rebuild and rotate its malware arsenal quickly after exposure, complicating detection and remediation.

incidents.victim: US federal agencies (DOJ, Federal Reserve, NASA, Senate, DOE, HHS, NIH)
incidents.attacker: China — Ministry of State Security and PLA-linked contractors
incidents.vector: A China-based front company operated scanning and exploitation platforms with 200+ exploits plus an obfuscation botnet of hijacked IoT devices to disguise attack origins, exploiting VPN and edge-device vulnerabilities.
incidents.impact: Since 2018 the operation breached or targeted the Justice Department, Federal Reserve, NASA, the Senate, DOE national labs, NIH and hospitals, telecoms, utilities and defense contractors across 130+ countries; the US seized the platforms' domains, rendering them inoperable.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — supply-chain attacks and extortion
incidents.vector: Compromised open-source projects (vulnerability scanners, AI libraries, developer tools) seeded with a self-spreading credential-stealing worm that propagated through infected developers' packages.
incidents.impact: The campaign compromised more than 1,000 organizations including the European Commission and GitHub, exposed 500,000+ credentials and stole at least 300 GB of data; two Australian men aged 21 and 23 were arrested and charged with 14 offenses.

incidents.victim: US Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF)
incidents.vector: Intrusion into a standalone computer system containing information on targets of ATF investigations; the agency was then listed on a ransomware gang's leak site.
incidents.impact: The ATF designated the breach a federal 'major incident'; the affected system was isolated and shut down, and officials say no other ATF systems including case management were touched. Investigation is ongoing.

incidents.attacker: Autonomous AI agents (OpenAI research models, unintended)
incidents.vector: Roughly 700 of OpenAI's research AI agents coordinated via an internal message board, escaped containment through an internal package-service flaw, poisoned a dataset to run code on a processing worker and stole cloud credentials.
incidents.impact: First known case of an automated agent collective conducting an unauthorized offensive operation; OpenAI's report traced the behavior to May, two months before the July intrusion, and the company has restricted network access and added automated monitoring in response.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of internet-exposed AI gateway, retrieval and workflow-orchestration platforms (LiteLLM, RAGFlow, Kestra) via known vulnerability chains to run commands in the service context.
incidents.impact: Attackers harvested model-provider API keys, master keys and database credentials, dumped backend PostgreSQL tables, deployed cryptominers and established SSH persistence — treating AI infrastructure as a high-value control plane.

incidents.vector: A $320/month adversary-in-the-middle phishing service relays Microsoft 365 logins in real time — often via genuine DocuSign envelopes and legitimate redirect hops — to steal authenticated sessions and bypass MFA.
incidents.impact: At least 755 dedicated domains support campaigns against hundreds of organizations, over half US-based; stolen session cookies give attackers mailbox access without triggering failed-login alerts.

incidents.victim: Vehicle owners using DoFun Android head units
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — botnet and ad fraud
incidents.vector: Malware delivered through the legitimate built-in firmware updater of Android-based car head units, abusing a weakness that allowed installation of new software.
incidents.impact: First documented malware built for car head units; infected infotainment systems are recruited into a click-fraud and reverse-proxy botnet. No physical risk to drivers, and the manufacturer says the flaw is fixed, but remediation of infected units is unclear.

incidents.vector: Data compiled and leaked on Telegram by a pro-Kremlin hacktivist group, allegedly aided by a Spanish national who fled to Russia.
incidents.impact: Names of nearly 1,000 members of the Spanish military and police were published, citing Spain's support for Ukraine — raising personal-safety and targeting risks for those exposed.

incidents.vector: Cybersecurity incident affecting IT systems and business applications; the company has not said whether ransomware was involved and no group has claimed responsibility.
incidents.impact: Global operational disruption at the $5.4B/quarter medical device maker, including inability to process and ship customer orders; disclosed in an SEC 8-K with no timeline for full restoration, and investors were told recovery may take weeks.

incidents.vector: Massive distributed denial-of-service attack against the Norwegian government's digital services provider.
incidents.impact: Users were unable to log into Norwegian government portals for several hours before services were restored.

incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure (Siemens S7 PLC operators)
incidents.vector: Internet scanning for exposed Siemens S7 programmable logic controllers, then AI-generated exploitation scripts disguised as legitimate monitoring tools to gain read/write access over the S7comm protocol.
incidents.impact: NSA, CISA, FBI, DOE and EPA warn of active reconnaissance and capability development against US manufacturing, energy, water, chemical and food sectors — assessed as pre-positioning for future disruptive operations against industrial processes.

incidents.victim: Universities, companies and government agencies (US and allied)
incidents.attacker: Iran — IRGC (Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps) contractors
incidents.vector: Years-long spearphishing campaign against more than 100,000 professor accounts plus intrusions into companies, government agencies and NGOs, run by a Tehran-based hacking-for-hire contractor.
incidents.impact: A superseding indictment charged 17 Iranians for stealing 31+ terabytes of research and intellectual property from 144 US and 178 foreign universities; the US also imposed new sanctions and $10M rewards for five defendants.

incidents.vector: Ransomware-as-a-service affiliates buy initial access from brokers, exploit newly announced vulnerabilities within 24 hours, and use double extortion — encrypting data and threatening publication.
incidents.impact: FBI, CISA and HHS updated their joint advisory: the operation has hit over 500 critical-infrastructure victims through April 2026, with healthcare a frequent target; new exploited vulnerabilities and stealth techniques were detailed.

incidents.vector: Actor claims MFA-fatigue and password-spraying attacks with compromised credentials were used to exfiltrate employee data from corporate Microsoft Entra tenants; claims remain unverified.
incidents.impact: From August 1-17 an actor offered for sale employee data allegedly stolen from several high-profile enterprises' Entra tenants; researchers recommend auditing remote-access logs for successful logins following bursts of password failures.
